profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer at Netflix
profile.summary: I am a principle engineer with over 30 years of experience designing and implementing high quality, scalable products.  While I have done UI work with JSPs, JavaScript, and HTML, my main focus has been on backend server components and infrastructure.  I have seen a lot of poorly designed and badly written code and therefore I’m highly motivation to produce well structured, well documented, thoroughly tested, and easily maintained components.  My main goals are to work on interesting projects that are of real-world value and to stay current with emerging technologies in order to exploit them where they make sense.

positions.title: Technical Yahoo
positions.description:
I was one of three people hand selected from the Tiger Team by the CTO to help evaluate various open source cloud infrastructures. On our recommendation, OpenStack was chosen as Yahoo’s internal cloud platform.

Jack of all trades. When a new component or functionality is needed, frequently I am the “go to” guy to investigate, prototype a proof of concept and evaluate the performance and/or potential impact. My boss has frequently told me that she appreciates my ability to quickly jump on something and with little guidance, come up to speed as this allows her to keep the rest of the team focused on longer term projects.

I was responsible for the design and implementation of our deployment process. The first two generations used internal Yahoo tools and the current third generation is being done with Chef

Yahoo put together a team of high performers to work on a special ad serving project. I was hand selected by one of Yahoo’s top managers who was put in charge. In additional to my coding duties, I was the team lead for the my component, coordinating the actions of three developers with the rest of the project.

Member of Yahoo’s Flex Force “Tiger” team

Worked on wide range of projects that ranged from 3 to 9 months in length. (E.g. Ad server, apache traffic server, Yahoo Distributed Hash Tables, Mobile Apps, Hadoop Map/Reduce)

Worked on a number of internal Tiger projects (E.g. designing data warehousing schema to analyze individual Tiger assignments, usage, and effectiveness. I also developed and presented a 3 day introduction to writing Mobile Apps (IOS and Android) based on my own self-study.)

Designed, implemented, and tested the User Profile Service that was used within Yahoo! for a number of years before the service was retired. At its peak, it was handling 1,000,000 requests per second.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Jack of all trades. This company went from eighty employees down to three before it shutdown completely. I was one of the final three.

Design, implemented, tested a wide range of functional components. Cleaned up the existing code base and optimized the database usage.

Mentored junior members of the team.

Respond immediately to key customer issues on functionality and performance.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
Design, prototype, implement, test, and support many core components. 

Quickly and cheerfully respond to the needs of the business.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Many, many, many improvements to functionality and performance. It’s about what you’d expect for a person that was on the development team when it only had three engineers and then grew to over twenty.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description: Worked on a preprocessors for embedded SQL and DBD (Data Base Deduction) statements in a C program along with the client/server components.

positions.title: Senior Associate Programmer
positions.description:
Worked in Knowledge Based Systems group designing, coding, and testing portions of Knowledge Tool and IBM's version of Common Lisp.

Worked on the VM/XA release. (Received IBM's highest performance rating.)

SQL/DS VSE System Tester

projects.title: OpenStack
projects.description: Integrating OpenStack into Yahoo!, contributing code and architecture based on the kind of Mega-Scale we deal with at Yahoo! back to the awesome OpenStack community.
